category: market data API (end-of-day stock prices, tickers, exchanges)

free_tier.stated: Free plan USD 0/month, free forever: 100 requests per month, end-of-day data, 1 year of history, no support
free_tier.notes: Each symbol in a request consumes one request, up to 100 symbols per call, and a page holds up to 1000 rows. The APILayer product page shows the free plan as 100 Total Requests while its FAQ on the same page says 100 per month; the marketstack.com pricing page and FAQ say per month. The cheapest paid plan is Basic at USD 8.99/month billed yearly with 10,000 requests per month. US end-of-day prices are licensed from Tiingo.

per_object_cap.stated: 1000 rows per page and 100 symbols per call; 1 year of history on the free plan

retention.stated: not applicable: a query API with no stored objects

egress.terms: not metered in bytes; the 100 requests a month bound what a free key can pull

interface_detail: GET https://api.marketstack.com/v2/eod?access_key=...&symbols=AAPL over HTTPS on every plan; v1 paths remain. A call with no access_key answered HTTP 401 missing_access_key.
chaining: Its US end-of-day prices are licensed from Tiingo, whose free plan allows 1000 requests a day against 100 a month here, so Tiingo is the larger free route to the same prices.

limits.value: 100 requests per month on the free plan; each symbol in a request counts as one
5 requests per second (documentation as archived on 2026-01-13)
1000 rows per page, 100 symbols per call

limits_note: History window: 1 year on the free plan, 10 years on Basic, 15+ years above; no limits[] kind names a history window. Bulk path: no bulk path.
binding_note: 100 a month, with each symbol counted, is spent long before the 5 per second rate or the row caps matter.

identity_cost.detail: The free signup form asks for a first name, last name, email and password, and under Billing Details an address, postal code, country and city (state optional); no card field was seen on the free form. Card payment is named for paid plans.

reliability_note: Past the monthly volume the API answers HTTP 429 too_many_requests, and past the rate it answers 429 rate_limit_reached.
confidence_note: The free quota, history and signup fields are documented on the pricing, FAQ and signup pages; the 5 per second rate is from the documentation as archived on 2026-01-13, because the current documentation pages read did not state it. A probe measured that a call with no key answers HTTP 401. The monthly cut-off needs a free key to measure.
